resources.string: ElevenLabs Scribe turns your speech into text as you talk; Claude can then tidy it up. Your audio and text go to those services under your own API keys, which are stored encrypted on this phone.
Allow the microphone in Voicebar settings
Needs speech-to-text access. Create one at elevenlabs.io under Developers → API keys.
Removes filler words, fixes punctuation and applies spoken corrections (\"Tuesday, no, Wednesday\"). Create a key at console.anthropic.com.
The fastest model works best here.
Paste a new key to replace the saved one
Couldn\'t store the key securely on this phone
Words appear in the text field as you talk, and the polished version replaces them when it\'s ready. Off: words preview in the voice bar and are typed when you finish. Password fields always preview.

Millennial mode: dictated messages never end with a period, because a final period reads as cold. Question marks, exclamation marks and periods between sentences stay. Keep talking after a message and its period comes back before the new words.
Messaging apps (Messages, WhatsApp, Signal, Slack…) and any box whose Enter key sends. Email, notes and everything else keep their periods.
No final period in any field.
While dictating, say “voice bar” and a command as the last thing, then pause. The command runs and isn\'t typed.

While a keyboard is up and you\'re not dictating (Voicebar\'s bar, or Gboard with the way-back button), the phone listens for “voice bar”. The button turns purple; “…listen” (or dictate, start, talk) starts dictating, switching back from Gboard if needed; “…close” (or hide) puts the keyboard away. Runs on the phone, nothing is sent anywhere, and the mic indicator stays on while it listens. Now: %1$s

“Voice bar, done”: finish (polished)
“Voice bar, send”: finish, then send
“Voice bar, keyboard”: finish, then Gboard
“Voice bar, clean up”: polish so far, keep listening
“Voice bar, cancel”: throw it away
“Voice bar, close”: finish, then hide the keyboard
Loose wording works too: “finish”, “send it”, “type”, “polish”, “never mind”, “scratch that”…

Dictation finishes by itself after this long without a recognized word (background noise doesn\'t count). Halfway there (at most 5 seconds in) what you\'ve said so far is cleaned up while it keeps listening; keep talking and the next cleanup sees both, so corrections still work.
Layout, typing with Gboard, the way back
Names and terms it has learned · %1$d

When you fix a name or term in what Voicebar typed (here or in Gboard), Claude checks whether it\'s worth remembering, and it\'s added here with a note you can tap to undo. Rewording and ordinary edits are ignored; password fields are never read.
Sends your 50 most used words to ElevenLabs with each dictation so they\'re heard right the first time (ElevenLabs charges a little extra for this). The cleanup always gets the whole dictionary.
Stored on this phone only. Learned mishearings are fixed by the cleanup with context; ones you added, or that came up twice, are also replaced every time.
Millennial mode, in chats or everywhere
A text box to practice in
Add an ElevenLabs key to start
A few quick steps: Voicebar for talking, Gboard for typing, and a button on Gboard that brings you back.
Tap Voice and talk. ABC hands you to Gboard for typing; tap Tap to return on Gboard to come back.
Drag to move the cursor · hold still, then drag to select
Selecting · keep a finger down, drag with another to go further
no list price known for that model, so its tokens are counted but not priced

Estimated from what this phone sent, at list prices: Scribe v2 Realtime at $%1$.2f per hour of audio, and %2$s at %3$s. Plan allowances, free hours and credits aren\'t taken into account, so your actual bill can be lower; the ElevenLabs and Claude Console dashboards have the real numbers. Only counts are kept here, never your words or audio.
Create one at elevenlabs.io under Developers → API keys, with speech-to-text access, and paste it here.
Create one at console.anthropic.com under API keys and paste it here.

Tap Voice and talk; the words go straight into the field. Pause and what you\'ve said is polished while it keeps listening. Tap the pill to finish (always polished), swipe it right to finish and send, or swipe it left to throw it away. ⌫ keeps working while you talk. Or say “voice bar, done” (or send, keyboard, clean up, cancel) at the end. It also finishes by itself after a stretch of silence. Slide sideways on the idle Voice pill to move the cursor.

Tap ⌫ to delete a character; tap then hold to keep deleting. With three wide buttons, holding ⌫ opens return, space and delete under your finger; with seven equal buttons, space and return are on the bar and holding ⌫ keeps deleting.
Tap Voice and talk; tap ABC to type with Gboard.
Cursor, keyboard and voice in the middle. Hold delete for space and return.
Space and return on the bar. Hold delete to keep deleting.
Off. Tap to turn on Voicebar in Accessibility settings (if Android says it\'s restricted, allow restricted settings in the app\'s App info first).
Gboard isn\'t turned on as a keyboard. Tap to open keyboard settings.
Turn on Gboard in Android\'s keyboard settings first

Voicebar\'s companion. Over Gboard it shows a button that switches back to Voicebar, and listens for “voice bar” there. While you dictate it reads the text on screen once, so names come out spelled as they appear, and it notices when you fix a word Voicebar typed, to learn it. In hands-free mode (“voice bar, hands free”) it reads the screen and taps, types and scrolls where you say. It never reads password fields. What it reads goes only to ElevenLabs and Claude, with your own keys, and only while you\'re dictating or using hands-free.
A strip in Gboard\'s own color, joined to its top edge, that says Tap to return
Covers Gboard\'s voice key wherever Gboard puts it. With Gboard\'s voice key off, it takes the right-hand mirror of Gboard\'s ⊞ button, if that spot is free.
A mic bubble above Gboard; drag it anywhere
Turned on. ABC switches to it for typing.

Tap Cursor for a trackpad: drag to move the cursor, hold still then drag to select, and keep one finger down while another drags to go further. Cut, copy, paste and delete sit above it. Tap Done to fold it away.
Settings, switch to another keyboard, and what dictation has cost this month.
Tap ABC and Gboard takes over for typing. Tap to return on Gboard (or the mic in its voice-key spot, or the floating mic) brings Voicebar back, already listening.
Turn on the way back from Gboard

When you start talking, the text on screen (the chat you\'re replying to, say) goes with your speech to ElevenLabs and Claude, so names are spelled as they appear there and sound-alikes are read in context. The whole screen needs the Gboard button (accessibility) on; without it, only the text box is used. Password fields are never read.
Listen as soon as a text box opens
Dictation starts by itself whenever you tap into a text field, as if you\'d tapped Voice. Not in password fields, and not while a physical keyboard is connected.
Way back from Gboard is off. Tap to turn it on
No commands for 5 minutes · hands-free off
Add your ElevenLabs key for hands-free
Couldn\'t work that out · try again
No text box to type in
Cursor’s in the middle · “cursor up”, then “tap”
Hands-free needs the Gboard button (accessibility) on

Say “voice bar, hands free” (or use the Quick Settings tile) to control the phone by voice: “tap Send”, “scroll down”, “type …”, “open Spotify”, “show numbers” then “tap 7”, “go ahead and reply to Siona saying I\'m late”. A cursor shows each tap. Sending, buying or deleting waits for “yes”. Say “stop” or tap the pill to end. Needs the accessibility service; streams to ElevenLabs while on (about $0.39 an hour) and turns off after 5 quiet minutes.
Also listen for “voice bar, hands free” when no keyboard is up, on the phone, with the model above. Uses some battery and keeps the microphone indicator on.

tap / click / long press <name or number> · show numbers · hide numbers · scroll up/down (a bit · half a screen · one full screen · two pages · a lot · to the top · all the way down) · page up/down · swipe left/right · zoom in/out · type <words> · clear · focus the search box · open <app or thing on screen> · go back · go home · recent apps · notifications · quick settings · cursor up/down/left/right (a bit) · cursor to <name> · tap · go ahead and <goal> · yes · no · stop. Anything else is worked out by Claude.
Skipped · you can add it in Settings
Talk instead of type. A one-row voice bar that sits under your apps; Gboard stays around for typing.
Voicebar for talking, Gboard for typing, one tap apart
Used only while you talk to it
ElevenLabs hears you; Claude tidies the words (optional). You pay them directly, usually pennies
Optional: a way back from Gboard, and hands-free control
About three minutes. Everything here can be changed later in Settings.
In the list that opens, turn on Voicebar, and Gboard if it\'s off. Then come back here.
Turn it on in the list
Not installed: Voicebar uses it for typing

Android warns that a keyboard can collect what you type. Voicebar doesn\'t record typing: it sends what you say to ElevenLabs, and the words to Claude for cleanup, with your own keys. Nothing goes anywhere else.
Pick Voicebar in the list that pops up. It\'ll be the keyboard you see first.
The keyboard button on the bar switches to Gboard; the Gboard button (later) brings you back
Voicebar listens only when you ask it to.
While you\'re dictating, or in hands-free mode; the bar shows it every time
Listening for the wake word happens on the phone; nothing is sent until you start talking to it
Voicebar uses ElevenLabs to hear you, with your own API key. It costs about $0.39 per hour of talking.
Make a free account; speech to text is billed by the hour as you use it
Opens Developers › API Keys. Tap Create, give it Speech to Text access, then copy it.
The key is checked with ElevenLabs, then kept on this phone, encrypted. It\'s never sent anywhere but ElevenLabs.
Claude fixes punctuation, drops the ums and spells your names right. Optional, but it\'s what makes the text sound like you wrote it.
“um so meet at the camel back trail head at six forty no wait seven”
Meet at the Camelback trailhead at 7.
New to the Claude API? Sign up
Opens the Claude Console. API use is separate from a Claude.ai Pro or Max plan
The API is pay as you go: a few dollars of credit lasts a long time for cleanup
Opens Settings › API keys. Tap Create key, then copy it (it starts with sk-ant-).
Uses Claude Haiku: a fraction of a cent per message. Kept on this phone, encrypted, and sent only to Anthropic.
Optional. Turn on Voicebar in Accessibility to put a button on Gboard that brings you back, and to unlock hands-free control.
Android blocks this for apps installed from a file, like this one. Allow it once:
Try turning Voicebar on in Accessibility first
In App info, tap ⋮ and then Allow restricted settings
Come back and turn it on again
A mic button on Gboard that switches back to Voicebar
“Voice bar, hands free”: tap, scroll and type by voice
Reads the screen as you start talking, and learns from your fixes in Gboard

Accessibility lets Voicebar see and act on what\'s on screen. It reads the screen only while you dictate or use hands-free, never password fields, and sends it only to ElevenLabs and Claude with your keys.
Tap any text box and Voicebar comes up. Tap the mic and talk.
Run this again any time from Settings › Help.
